records.name: Medical Care Research and Review
records.scope_notes: Fits existing-data analyses, evidence syntheses, and methodological brief reports about health service organization, financing, delivery, or related policy. A new contribution and conceptual framework are important; a generic disease-outcomes paper without a health-services connection is a poor fit.

route.conditions: Standard subscription publication. Optional Sage Choice open access and requested print color have charges; online color is free. Follow the relevant article-type word limit.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated for the standard route; no membership or page charge is imposed in the author instructions.

fee_evidence.note: Journal-specific policy explicitly states that submission and publication carry no fees; distinguishes optional open access and print color costs.

difficulty.basis: Not assessed in discovery; contribution criteria do not establish acceptance odds.

records.name: Journal of Health Services Research & Policy
records.scope_notes: Fits secondary analyses of health services and systems, policy analyses, systematic/scoping/realist reviews, and conceptual or methodological work. Authors must explain international relevance. Protocols are not accepted; unsolicited editorials are excluded.

route.conditions: Choose the standard subscription route. Optional open access and requested print color cost extra; online color is free. Article-type length and reporting requirements apply.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated for standard publication; no mandatory membership or page charge is identified.

fee_evidence.note: The journal expressly makes both submission and publication free and separates optional open access and print color.

difficulty.basis: Not assessed in discovery; no acceptance-rate evidence collected.

records.name: Health Services Management Research
records.scope_notes: Fits health-service organization and management analyses, substantial theoretical or methodological advances, and rigorous evidence syntheses. Existing-data studies should establish management implications and a contribution beyond a local description. The listed scientific article types have external peer review; perspectives and nonscientific pieces may follow different review requirements.

route.conditions: Standard subscription route; optional Sage Choice open access and specifically requested print color cost extra. Online color is free. Respect article-type limits.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated for standard publication; no membership or compulsory page charge is listed.

fee_evidence.note: Journal-specific instructions explicitly cover free submission and publication and identify optional open access and print color charges.

difficulty.basis: Not assessed in discovery; no measured acceptance probability claimed.

records.name: Health Information Management Journal
records.publisher: Sage; official research journal of the Health Information Management Association of Australia
records.scope_notes: Fits health-information management, coding, information quality, governance, and policy research using existing records or evidence synthesis. The journal welcomes international submissions. Research should improve knowledge or practice in health information management rather than simply report an unrelated predictive model.

route.conditions: Standard publication is free; open access is optional. Requested print color can cost extra; online color is available. Research articles normally have a 5,000-word limit, excluding abstract and references.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated; society membership is not required by the instructions, which invite authors worldwide.

fee_evidence.note: Official journal instructions explicitly state that submission and publication are free and describe open access and print color as optional.

difficulty.basis: Not assessed in discovery; no acceptance statistics collected.

records.name: Journal of Health Organization and Management
records.scope_notes: Fits theory-led analyses of healthcare organization, management, information systems, resource allocation, workforce, and governance; also accepts protocol-based reviews. The journal expects meaningful theoretical engagement and discourages superficial descriptive work. Its homepage provides journal-specific article limits.

route.conditions: Standard route; selecting gold open access incurs an APC. Optional self-archiving of the accepted manuscript is available under publisher policy.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None under the linked policy, which excludes financial contributions outside chosen gold open access.

fee_evidence.note: Directly linked by this journal: no submission fee; payment is requested only for chosen gold open access, not otherwise for publication, processing, or review.
Journal navigation links to the cited publisher author guidelines, establishing their applicability.

difficulty.basis: Not assessed in discovery; its theoretical-contribution criteria do not establish acceptance odds.

records.name: International Journal of Health Governance
records.scope_notes: Fits empirical, conceptual, comparative, and review work on health-system governance, digital health/data protection, quality metrics, resilience, and cross-sector coordination. Existing-data and synthesis projects should yield actionable governance insights. Journal-specific original articles and Health Governance Reviews have a 7,000-word limit.

route.conditions: Choose standard publication; gold open access is optional and carries an APC. Follow the journal's article-type requirements.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None under the linked author guidelines; payment is confined to chosen gold open access.

fee_evidence.note: This journal links to the guidelines: no submission payment or other publication, processing, or review payment unless gold open access is chosen.
The journal's author-guidelines navigation points directly to the cited policy.

difficulty.basis: Not assessed in discovery; no acceptance-rate value retained.

records.name: Health Care Management Science
records.scope_notes: Strong fit for computational health-service operations, queueing, scheduling, simulation, analytics, productivity, and policy models with a clear decision focus and practical relevance. Routine applications are discouraged. Reviews are limited, emphasize methods, and authors are encouraged to check with the journal; bibliometric analyses are low priority.

route.conditions: The journal expressly offers subscription publication without APCs. Submission fees were not explicitly resolved. Optional open access and print color carry costs; online color is free. Confirm absence of compulsory page/other charges before submission.
route.other_mandatory_costs: Unknown: no compulsory page or membership payment was found, but a complete explicit no-mandatory-cost statement was not obtained.

fee_evidence.note: Journal-specific publishing options expressly provide a subscription route without APCs; paid open access is a separate choice. This does not explicitly resolve submission fees.
Online color is free; print color requires an author contribution. No explicit submission-fee declaration was found in these instructions.

difficulty.basis: Not assessed in discovery; methodological novelty and practical impact are editorial criteria, not measured acceptance odds.

records.name: Journal of Medical Systems
records.scope_notes: Fits existing-data and methodological research on health-information systems, workflow engineering/simulation, implementation, operations, and governance. Brief Reports can describe tools, datasets, or pipelines with validation. Reviews need reproducible searches. Narrow algorithm comparisons and clinical studies with weak informatics contributions face desk rejection. Clinical interventions remain outside OSRI's initial scope.

route.conditions: Subscription publication has no APC; open access is optional and charged. Submission-fee status and complete compulsory-cost coverage remain unconfirmed. Instructions state that color illustrations are free.
route.other_mandatory_costs: Unknown: no mandatory membership/page fee was identified, but no explicit complete no-mandatory-cost statement was obtained.

fee_evidence.note: Journal-specific options state that no APC applies to subscription publication, with paid open access as a separate choice.
Color publication is free. Submission-fee status was not explicitly established by these instructions.

difficulty.basis: Not assessed in discovery; no measured acceptance probability collected.

records.name: International Journal of Medical Informatics
records.publisher: Elsevier; official journal of EFMI and IMIA
records.scope_notes: Fits health-information-system evaluation, interoperability, implementation/governance, and evidence synthesis about ICT in healthcare. The current publisher scope excludes bibliometrics, unevaluated conceptual architectures, and isolated algorithm performance without clinical translation. Nonclinical OSRI work would need a substantial evaluated systems contribution or rigorous synthesis using existing evidence.

route.conditions: Important candidate retained for fee audit. Official shop page confirms subscription access and journal scope, but the journal's author/fee and insights pages returned HTTP 403. No verified zero-cost author route is claimed.
route.other_mandatory_costs: Unknown; submission, standard publication, page/length, and membership costs need journal-specific verification.

fee_evidence.note: HTTP 403 prevented inspection of the journal-specific author and cost policy.
Official publisher shop establishes a subscription offering and scope, not the absence of author fees.

difficulty.basis: Not assessed in discovery; official author and peer-review policy could not be retrieved.

records.name: Health Policy
records.scope_notes: Fits original research and reviews evaluating health policies, reform processes, and cross-country health-system comparisons using quantitative or qualitative evidence. Focus is high-income countries, primarily outside the US; clear international policy implications are required. Publisher and Observatory collaboration pages establish the health-systems scope.

route.conditions: Major policy venue retained pending journal-specific fee verification. Official shop confirms subscription access, but author and insights pages returned HTTP 403. A reader subscription option alone does not establish free submission/publication.
route.other_mandatory_costs: Unknown; page/length, submission, publication, and any other compulsory author costs remain unresolved.

fee_evidence.note: Journal-specific author instructions returned HTTP 403; no fee-free claim is inferred from this unavailable page.
Official shop confirms subscription access and policy scope but does not state the author's compulsory costs.

difficulty.basis: Not assessed in discovery; journal-specific author and peer-review policy was blocked.

notes: Six records have explicit official evidence covering both submission and standard publication without a selective waiver; all six free routes are subscription routes, not diamond open access.

The two Springer journals explicitly confirm subscription publication without APCs. Submission fees and complete compulsory-cost coverage remain unresolved, so they are conservatively needs_verification.

ScienceDirect journal policy pages returned HTTP 403 for the two Elsevier candidates. Official publisher shop pages were readable and supplied current scope. Fees and journal-specific peer-review details remain unknown pending independent audit.

The current International Journal of Medical Informatics scope is substantially implementation-focused. Isolated modeling, bibliometrics, and unimplemented architectures should not be represented as good fits.
No acceptance rates, citation metrics, or difficulty rankings are asserted. Publisher shop impact values were undated and were deliberately not copied.

Requested print color, optional open access, and optional editing services are distinct from mandatory standard publication costs. Permission/licensing costs for third-party content, if chosen by an author, are not assessed here.
Discovery is a venue catalog for OSRI's nonclinical existing-data, computational, and synthesis work. It is not manuscript-specific matching or human scientific review.
The older emeraldgrouppublishing.com journal pages were blocked on direct fetch; current emerald.com journal pages and their directly linked June 2026 author guidance were readable and used instead.
